messages:
felix: alert-bot just paged oncall — gateway 5xx jump in eu-west and ap-south, started ~03:22 UTC. Observed 5xx fraction ~3.6% at peak. :rotating_light:
alert-bot: ALERT -> gateway_5xx_high firing for scope=region=eu-west,expr: (sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="gateway",status=~"5.."}[5m]))/sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="gateway"}[5m]))) > 0.025 and sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="gateway"}[5m])) > 120, for: 2m.
anya: I'm on. No platform deploys in the last hour. I see a bunch of 502/504 coming from edge -> origin pool eu-origins-b. Access logs show connect_timeout and recv_reset patterns.
mike: same. Also metrics show gateway_retries_total spiking in lockstep with origin_errors_total — retry amplification likely.
zara: Can we flip gateway to fail-fast and reduce retry attempts? Also throttle concurrency to the eu-origin pool.
felix: Applying quick mitigation: set GATEWAY_RETRIES=0 and ORIGIN_MAX_CONN=60 via configmap, rolling restart on the gateway in eu-west cluster. Command: `kubectl set env deploy/gateway GATEWAY_RETRIES=0 ORIGIN_MAX_CONN=60 --namespace=prod-eu-west`
alert-bot: NOTE -> config change detected by deploy-bot at 2045679051 (user: felix).
anya: While mitigation rolls, the pager is very chatty. The alert uses a short window and ratio-only which pages on low qps spikes. Can we add absolute-count gating and a longer for: value?
sre-manager: Agree. Quick emergency patch proposal from me: require both ratio + absolute count over longer window to reduce noise. Proposed expr:
```
# emergency: require >0.018 ratio over 15m AND >200 reqs/5m
(expr: (sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="gateway",status=~"5.."}[15m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="gateway"}[15m]))) > 0.018 and sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="gateway"}[5m])) > 200)
for: 6m
```
I'll push this as an emergency rule; monitoring team please review post-incident.
mike: Also propose excluding when upstream_health{upstream=~"eu-origin.*"} == 0 (provider-side outage). We still want to record events but not page ops for upstream provider-wide failures.
zara: For triage, dash-bot can you spin up a focussed dashboard showing: 1) 5xx fraction and absolute counts, 2) gateway_retries_total vs origin_errors_total, 3) upstream_health (0/1) over time, 4) per-upstream 504 heatmap?
dash-bot: Created temp dashboard "gateway-5xx-triage-2045" link: https://grafana.redwood/d/hjk321/gateway-5xx-triage-2045. Panels created: 10 (5xx frac), 11 (absolute counts), 12 (retry vs origin errors), 13 (upstream_health), 14 (504 heatmap). Runbook card added to panel 15.
felix: I'll apply the emergency alert patch now to stop noisy pages.
alert-bot: NOTE -> Emergency alert override applied by sre-manager at 2045679105. Old rule muted for eu-west and ap-south.
anya: Customer-impact check: customer-success — any customer reports?
customer-success: CS reports a handful of EU customers saw transient 502/504 errors between 03:21-03:40 UTC. No escalations yet. Most traffic retried successfully. We'll prep a short status note if this persists.
mike: After the fast-fail mitigation the 5xx fraction is trending down. Circuit-breaker activation reduced origin load. Will keep observing for 15-30m.
zara: Action items for post-incident: 1) turn this emergency rule into a permanent refinement in monitoring repo (include absolute count gating, longer window, and upstream_health exclusion), 2) add synthetic origin check (simple HTTP probe) and export upstream_health metric so alerts can correlate, 3) create a non-paging 'provider-outage' alert that records events without paging, 4) add dashboard panel with alert firing history vs traffic to detect false positives.
sre-manager: I'll own the monitoring PR and retro. Create ticket MON-945 and include timeline, logs, mitigation commands, dashboard link, and suggested alert edits. Please include a unit test harness that simulates low-qps high-ratio bursts to ensure we don't page.
anya: Also recommend moving to SLO-driven paging for critical paths: alert based on error_budget_burn (metric: slo_error_budget_burn{service="gateway",region=..}) > 0.1 over 30m OR absolute 5xx > threshold. That ties pages to product impact rather than raw ratio.
mike: Agree, SLO-based rules reduce noise and prioritize customer impact.
sre-manager: PR created: https://git.redwood/monitoring/alerts/pull/524 (emergency override + followup PR outline). Ticket MON-945 opened and assigned to monitoring and platform.
dash-bot: Updated dashboard with permanent panel ids and linked runbook: https://grafana.redwood/d/hjk321/gateway-5xx-triage-2045?orgId=1
felix: Handing off follow-up to zara for runbook/dashboards and to sre-manager for monitoring rule changes. I'll keep watching metrics for another hour.
customer-success: We'll prepare a short note for affected customers summarizing mitigation and next steps if you want to share later.
zara: On it. I'll include exact PromQL in the ticket and the dashboard card. Proposed PromQL examples to include in MON-945:
```
# absolute 5xx count by upstream
sum by (upstream) (rate(http_requests_total{service="gateway",status=~"5.."}[5m]))

# ratio with upstream_health exclusion
( sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="gateway",status=~"5..",upstream!~"eu-origin.*|provider-x"}[15m]))
/ sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="gateway",upstream!~"eu-origin.*|provider-x"}[15m])) )

# slo error budget burn
slo_error_budget_burn{service="gateway",region=~"eu-.*|ap-.*"}
```
sre-manager: Scheduling a postmortem next Tue. Please attach any logs/snippets to MON-945. Handoff complete: zara owns dashboards/runbook, sre-manager owns monitoring changes. Closing pager, thanks team :white_check_mark:
